name: sol_integrations_ac_6
description: Aave flash loan fee inflates pool liquidity index, allowing index manipulation via repeated flash loans
question: The source file in `source` integrates with Aave (e.g., calls flashLoan, flashLoanSimple, or reads Aave reserve liquidity index/normalized income) and uses the Aave pool's liquidity index or scaled balances as a price or accounting reference without accounting for the fact that repeated flash loans within a single block can inflate that index, allowing an attacker to manipulate the index value that the integration relies on; this does not apply to code that only interacts with Aave for simple deposit/withdraw without reading or relying on the liquidity index for pricing or accounting decisions.
criteria: A function computes a share price or exchange rate directly from Aave's getReserveNormalizedIncome() or liquidityIndex within the same block as a flash loan call, without any time-weighting or averaging

A vault or strategy contract uses the current Aave scaled balance / liquidity index ratio as the sole basis for minting or redeeming shares, letting an attacker inflate the index via self-issued flash loans before redeeming
Reward or interest calculations read Aave's reserve index in real time and use it to settle user balances without checking for anomalous single-block jumps caused by flash loan fees
